payload.question:
"A judge question that forgets its records still reaches the owner" changed since you answered "Yes: it reaches the owner without the You said line; only missing options or plumb's internal words trigger the retry" to "Is a judge question with no quote of the owner's words usable?". Does your answer still hold for what it says now?

Then: The judge's answer format requires each question to name the records it settles; when a question still comes back without them, plumb takes the records of the job instead of rejecting it. A question without a quote of the owner's words is usable: it reaches the owner without the "You said" line. Only a question missing its options or using plumb's internal words is retried once; still unusable after the retry, it goes to a debug case and its records keep waiting until the debug case fixes the question. The verdicts already given are applied.
EX-1: given the judge answers like the 2026-10-16 job: three questions, each without the records it settles, when plumb reads the answer, then the three questions reach the owner through the question tool and no verdict waits
EX-2: given the judge's answer format given to the model, when the judge model is asked, then the format is lenient, a question needs only its text, and the judge's instructions and plumb's retry enforce the records and 2 to 4 options (DEC-208)
EX-3: given a question with one option only, when plumb reads it, then the job is retried once; if it fails again a debug case is written, the question's records keep waiting, and the other verdicts are applied
EX-4: given a question with options but no quote of the owner's words, when plumb reads it, then it reaches the owner without the "You said" line and is not retried

Now: The judge's answer format requires each question to name the records it settles; when a question still comes back without them, plumb takes the records of the job instead of rejecting it. A question without a quote of the owner's words is usable: it reaches the owner without the "You said" line. Only a question missing its options is retried once (one using plumb's internal words reaches the agent marked to reword it, SR-362); still unusable after the retry, it goes to a debug case and its records keep waiting until the debug case fixes the question. The verdicts already given are applied.
EX-1: given the judge answers like the 2026-10-16 job: three questions, each without the records it settles, when plumb reads the answer, then the three questions reach the owner through the question tool and no verdict waits
EX-2: given the judge's answer format given to the model, when the judge model is asked, then the format is lenient, a question needs only its text, and the judge's instructions and plumb's retry enforce the records and 2 to 4 options (DEC-208)
EX-3: given a question with one option only, when plumb reads it, then the job is retried once; if it fails again a debug case is written, the question's records keep waiting, and the other verdicts are applied
EX-4: given a question with options but no quote of the owner's words, when plumb reads it, then it reaches the owner without the "You said" line and is not retried

What changed: DEC-192 says a question using plumb's internal words triggers the retry, but the requirement now retries only a question missing its options and sends internal-word questions to the agent marked for rewording (SR-362), and the later DEC-162 doesn't cover that point.

It comes from your decision "Is a judge question with no quote of the owner's words usable?" of 2026-10-18 under your request "plumb keeps itself fit at every landing, and parallel loops stay..." (The owner answered through the question tool on 2026-10-17.).
payload.reason: The owner settled this on 2026-10-24: a question using plumb's own words was set aside to the band, and they said "Yes but it wrongly shows the question in the band, not using the question tool?" and reported the plumb-video question "set aside (a question names plumb's own words)" as the bug. So such a question goes to the agent to reword (SR-362 EX-5) instead of being retried; only a missing-options question is retried. DEC-192's retry of plumb-worded questions is what they called wrong.
